name: qualify-revise-fanout-py
note: Expected: good, good-workers, and batch16 pass (good-workers replaces the per-unit client in check with keep-alive worker connections, a different fix from good's thread pool over the existing client; batch16 reads in batches of 16 that each wait for their slowest unit, slower than a pool but within the 20 seconds on these datasets); noop (the fixture's correct sequential check) fails within_budget only; sequential-tweak (still one unit at a time, a reused connection and a 1.5 s wait) fails within_budget, and answered_units_correct and failures_handled too (the 1.5 s wait reports the edge units as no answer); two and three (good's pool with 2 or 3 workers) fail within_budget only (three can be within the 20 seconds on an ordinary day, never in the outage); patch-only (still one at a time, stops reading at 17 s and reports the rest as no answer) fails within_budget, answered_units_correct, and failures_handled; unbounded (a thread per unit) and default-pool (the executor's default size, 32 with the check's PYTHON_CPU_COUNT) fail within_limit and the two report checks (the gateway answers 429 past 16); abandoned-daemon (each read given up after 2 s in a daemon thread that keeps its connection) fails within_limit and the two report checks and may also fail no_held_requests; pool-holds (16 workers that stay on silent units' requests for 30 s, the main thread deciding no answer from when each read began) fails no_held_requests and within_budget; cut15 (the cutoff moved to 1.5 s) fails answered_units_correct and failures_handled; cut3 (moved to 3 s) fails failures_handled only; over-reach (check fixed as good does, temp moved onto the same parallel reader) and temp-continue (temp on a pool, printing every unit that answered and each failure on stderr) fail existing_commands_unchanged only; temp-timeout (the client's reads give up after 2 s by default, so temp does too) and units-format (units without the zone) fail existing_commands_unchanged only; wrong (lines in completion order) fails answered_units_correct only. Command arms need no toolchain: the check runs everything. The run is invalid on a host where the check sees 16 CPUs or fewer, or where the reference client's best time is more than 1.5 times the seconds it spends waiting on the gateway.
